questions.q: What do batch normalization and layer normalization both do, structurally?
options: Remove a layer's weights entirely
Normalize some group of activations to roughly zero mean and unit variance, then apply a learned scale and shift
Randomly zero out activations during training
Replace the optimizer with a different one
questions.explain: Both layers normalize a group of activations and then apply learned gamma/beta parameters to rescale and shift the result — they differ only in which activations get grouped together.

questions.q: Across which dimension does `nn.BatchNorm2d` compute its normalization statistics?
options: Across the batch dimension, separately for each channel
Across the feature dimension of a single sample
Across the width and height of a single image only
Across the entire dataset at once, recomputed every step
questions.explain: BatchNorm2d computes mean and variance across the batch dimension for each channel, which is why its behavior depends on batch size and composition.

questions.q: Why does `nn.LayerNorm` suit transformer and sequence models particularly well?
options: It requires a fixed, large batch size to work correctly
It normalizes per sample across the feature dimension, so it is unaffected by batch size or composition
It disables itself automatically during inference
It only works with convolutional layers
questions.explain: LayerNorm normalizes each sample independently across its feature dimension, making it insensitive to batch size — useful where batch composition varies, as in many sequence models.

questions.q: What does `nn.BatchNorm2d` use when the model is switched to `model.eval()`?
options: A freshly computed mean and variance from the current batch
The stored running mean and variance accumulated during training
A mean and variance of exactly 0 and 1 with no learned scale
Whatever LayerNorm's statistics were in the previous layer
questions.explain: At eval time, BatchNorm2d switches from the current batch's statistics to the running mean and variance it accumulated during training.

questions.q: Based on this lesson's guidance, which normalization layer would be the more natural default for a transformer processing batches whose size and composition vary a lot between steps?
options: nn.BatchNorm2d, because it adapts well to any batch size
nn.LayerNorm, because it normalizes per sample and is unaffected by batch size
Neither — transformers never use normalization layers
nn.Dropout, since it replaces normalization entirely
questions.explain: LayerNorm's per-sample normalization makes it insensitive to batch size and composition, which is exactly why it's the standard choice in transformer architectures.
